No. At that time and location, the Moon’s center is about **31.3° below the horizon**, so it is geometrically far out of sight. Atmospheric refraction near the horizon can shift apparent positions by only roughly **0.5°**, nowhere near enough to make it visible.

With the Sun also well below the horizon, the sky is dark—but that does not matter because the Earth itself blocks your view of the Moon. You would **not be able to spot it unaided**, even with perfectly clear skies.
